title: The collector and the settings that send to it
bridge: The OTel Collector is like a backend-for-frontend in front of an analytics API. Every client posts to one place, and it reshapes the data before forwarding. Except it deletes fields on purpose, so even a misconfigured client cannot store a prompt. And it checks a token before it reads a byte.
intro: Claude Code and the Agent SDK already export cost, tokens and tool decisions over OpenTelemetry, but today nothing receives them. This lesson deploys the collector that receives them on inf and scrubs content in one place. Every laptop and agent VM gets one address and one token. By the end, cost by team shows in Grafana with no names and no prompts.

picture.caption: One address, one token, one scrub: from a laptop to a team-level number in Grafana.

steps.text: posts OTLP over HTTPS with Authorization: Bearer <ingest token>
the WAF lets only /v1/metrics and /v1/logs through
an ExternalSecret gives INGEST_TOKEN and USER_SALT; the team map was rendered at apply time
checks the token, drops prompt and file_path, swaps email for team, writes metrics
writes events the same way, scrubbed
cost by team appears within a minute; no email anywhere

sections.h: A signal with nowhere to go
p: Set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 and Claude Code starts exporting metrics and events over OTLP (lesson p6-1). OTLP is the OpenTelemetry wire protocol; we use its HTTP form with protobuf bodies. Today those exports have no address to go to, so we lose them.

This lesson builds the receiving side in three tickets. G1-02 runs an OpenTelemetry Collector on inf-rhinohealth: two pods that take OTLP in, scrub it, and write on. G1-04 gives the collector a public address, otel.example.com. G1-05 points every Claude Code, on laptops and in agent VMs, at that address through managed settings.
Metrics go to VictoriaMetrics and events go to the long-term VictoriaLogs, kept for 1 year. There is no traces pipeline: inf has no trace store yet.

callout.text: No prompt, command or file path is stored, even from a misconfigured client. The collector scrubs in one place so that holds for everyone.

p: The collector is deployed like n8n (lesson p5-2): a helm_release of the upstream open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector chart, inside a module, modules/otel-collector. The chart's values come from a Terraform template file, so Terraform can fill in endpoints and the team map. This block is the first half: how the pods receive.
The ingest token is a shared secret every sender must present. The collector checks it with the bearertokenauth extension, which reads the token from an environment variable.
sections.because: We take the token from the environment rather than from the values file, so the rendered values never contain a secret.

code.text:
mode: deployment
replicaCount: 2
image:
  repository: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib   # contrib: transform processor and bearertokenauth
extraEnvsFrom:
  - secretRef: { name: otel-collector }              # ExternalSecret from kvv2 infrastructure/otel-collector
config:
  extensions:
    bearertokenauth: { token: "$${env:INGEST_TOKEN}" }
  receivers:
    otlp:
      protocols:
        http: { endpoint: "0.0.0.0:4318", auth: { authenticator: bearertokenauth } }
  processors:
    memory_limiter: { check_interval: 1s, limit_percentage: 80, spike_limit_percentage: 20 }

notes.text: deployment mode: a normal Deployment, not one pod per node. Senders come from outside the cluster.
Two replicas, so a restart does not drop telemetry.
The contrib image has the transform processor and bearertokenauth; the core image does not.
extraEnvsFrom loads a Kubernetes Secret as environment variables. An ExternalSecret fills it from kvv2 infrastructure/otel-collector (lesson p5-3).
Terraform's templatefile reads ${ as its own interpolation. $$ writes a literal ${env:INGEST_TOKEN}, which the collector resolves at start.
One receiver: OTLP over HTTP on port 4318, and every request must pass the authenticator first.
memory_limiter refuses data when memory passes 80 percent, so a burst cannot crash the pod.

p: The transform processor runs small statements on every record before export. Ours is named transform/scrub. It deletes the content attributes, replaces the person's email with a team name, and keeps a salted hash of the email. With the hash, weekly active users can be counted without names.

A salted hash is SHA-256 of the email plus a secret string, the salt. The same email always gives the same hash, so you can count distinct people. Nobody can turn the hash back into an email without the salt.

The team map, work email to team, lives in Vault at infrastructure/ai-agents/teams, and Sean fills it. A vault_kv_secret_v2 data source reads it, and the template's for loop writes one statement per person.
sections.because: We scrub in the collector, not on each client: one wrong env var on one laptop must not store a prompt.

code.text:
transform/scrub:
      error_mode: ignore
      log_statements:
        - context: log      # metric_statements repeat this list with context: datapoint
          statements:
            - delete_matching_keys(attributes, "^(prompt|prompt_text|user_system_prompt|full_command|file_path|tool_parameters)$")
%{ for email, team in teams ~}
            - set(attributes["team"], "${team}") where attributes["user.email"] == "${email}"
%{ endfor ~}
            - set(attributes["user.hash"], SHA256(Concat([attributes["user.email"], "$${env:USER_SALT}"], ""))) where attributes["user.email"] != nil
            - delete_key(attributes, "user.email")
    batch: {}
  exporters:
    otlphttp/metrics: { metrics_endpoint: "${metrics_endpoint}" }   # vminsert .../insert/0/opentelemetry/v1/metrics
    otlphttp/logs: { logs_endpoint: "${logs_endpoint}" }            # vlsingle-rhino-logs-longterm:9428
  service:
    extensions: [bearertokenauth]
    pipelines:
      metrics: { receivers: [otlp], processors: [memory_limiter, transform/scrub, batch], exporters: [otlphttp/metrics] }
      logs: { receivers: [otlp], processors: [memory_limiter, transform/scrub, batch], exporters: [otlphttp/logs] }

notes.text: error_mode: ignore: a statement that fails on one record is skipped for that record; the pipeline goes on.
log_statements apply to events. The same list is repeated as metric_statements with context: datapoint, so metrics are scrubbed too.
delete_matching_keys removes every attribute whose name matches: prompt, prompt_text, user_system_prompt, full_command, file_path, tool_parameters.
%{ for ... ~} is a Terraform template loop over the team map; ~ strips the line break. It is not YAML.
Rendered once per person: when user.email equals that email, set team. Terraform fills ${team} and ${email}.
user.hash is SHA256 of email plus salt. USER_SALT comes from the environment, so the rendered values hold no secret.
Then the email is deleted. After this line no record carries a name.
batch groups records before export: fewer, larger requests.
Metrics go to vminsert's OTLP insert path. Ask DevOps for -opentelemetry.usePrometheusNaming=true on vminsert, so series get names like claude_code_cost_usage_USD_total.
Events go to vlsingle-rhino-logs-longterm, the VictoriaLogs kept for 1 year.
Each pipeline runs the same three processors in order: limit memory, scrub, batch. There is no traces pipeline.

sections.h: Secrets, the unit and the proof
p: Terraform generates ingest_token and user_salt and writes them to kvv2 infrastructure/otel-collector, the way modules/n8n-secrets does. The ExternalSecret from vault-store turns that path into the Kubernetes Secret named otel-collector that the values load.
The unit lives at multi_tenant/accounts/infrastructure/otel-collector/terragrunt.hcl (lesson p4-2). A person runs plan and apply over VPN; agents never apply.

Prove the scrub twice. First from a pod with telemetrygen, a small tool that sends fake OTLP data. Then one real claude -p session with OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1 set on purpose: the prompt must not show up in VictoriaLogs.

Engineers are not always on VPN, and agent VMs have no peering to inf. So the collector gets a public HTTPS route, otel.example.com, behind Envoy's external gateway and the WAF. A WAF, a web application firewall, inspects each request and blocks known attack shapes. Ours is Coraza, and it fails closed like n8n's webhooks: when it cannot decide, it refuses.

Only two paths are open, /v1/metrics and /v1/logs. The collector checks the bearer token itself, and that token only lets you write telemetry. Test from a laptop off VPN with telemetrygen, with and without the token; without it you expect 401. If the WAF blocks protobuf bodies, add a rule exception for these two paths.
sections.because: We add the route to the same unit so the collector and its address are planned and applied together.

code.file: infrastructure/multi_tenant/accounts/infrastructure/otel-collector/terragrunt.hcl (the file-path comment and five blank lines dropped; nothing else)

notes.text: include root pulls in the shared root.hcl: remote state, providers, the Vault address. expose = true lets inputs read its locals.
The module from G1-02, by relative path, in the old tree's style.
Pin the chart release you tested. 0.0.0 is a placeholder to replace.
Where Terraform wrote ingest_token and user_salt.
Where Sean's team map lives; the module reads it with a vault_kv_secret_v2 data source.
vminsert's OTLP metrics insert path, in the metrics namespace from the root locals.
The long-term VictoriaLogs insert path on port 9428.
envoy-external is the internet-facing gateway, the same parent n8n's webhooks use.
Only two paths; a request to any other path never reaches the collector.
waf_fail_open = false: if the WAF cannot decide, the request is refused.

p: Server-managed settings are managed settings pushed from claude.ai to every laptop in the org (lesson p12-2 and lesson g0-6). The file 20-telemetry.json sits next to G0's 10-models.json. The people version is pasted into claude.ai with the real ingest token; the token never goes into git.

Team is not set here, because the file is org-wide and the collector turns the email into a team. Agents get a different copy, baked into the VM image by G3. It has no OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES, because the harness sets them per step, and no token.

The proposal for G3 is a small OTLP relay inside the LLM gateway. It checks the run token and adds the ingest token, so the VM holds no ingest token. Leave OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES and the traces exporter unset.
The check: on a laptop /status lists the managed source. Within a minute claude_code_cost_usage_USD_total appears in Grafana with a team label and no email.
sections.because: We turn telemetry on through managed settings so every laptop sends the same way, with content off at the source.

code.text:
{
  "$schema": "https://json.schemastore.org/claude-code-settings.json",
  "env": {
    "CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY": "1",
    "OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER": "otlp",
    "OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER": "otlp",
    "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL": "http/protobuf",
    "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT": "https://otel.example.com",
    "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS": "Authorization=Bearer <ingest token: set only in the admin console>",
    "OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS": "0",
    "OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES": "0",
    "OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS": "0",
    "OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT": "0",
    "OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_ACCOUNT_UUID": "false",
    "OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES": "department=rnd,source=human"
  }
}

notes.text: The master switch for Claude Code telemetry.
Metrics and events both go out as OTLP; the traces exporter stays unset.
http/protobuf: the HTTP form of OTLP, the one the collector's receiver and the WAF route accept.
The public address from G1-04; the exporter appends /v1/metrics and /v1/logs itself.
The placeholder is replaced with the real token only in the admin console, never in this file.
The four content flags off: no prompts, no assistant text, no tool details, no tool content.
No account UUID on metrics; the collector's user.hash is the only per-person key.
Resource attributes every laptop sends: department=rnd and source=human. Agents send source per step instead.

p: On the laptop you cannot use Terraform's template, so you write the rendered result by hand. It has two fake emails and a fake salt. The debug exporter prints every record to the terminal, so you can watch the scrub work. Note that tool_parameters is missing from the pattern; the faded step adds it.
sections.because: We use the debug exporter instead of otlphttp so the lab needs no VictoriaMetrics, only a terminal.

code.text:
extensions:
  bearertokenauth: { token: "lab-token" }
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http: { endpoint: "0.0.0.0:4318", auth: { authenticator: bearertokenauth } }
processors:
  transform/scrub:
    error_mode: ignore
    log_statements:
      - context: log
        statements:
          - delete_matching_keys(attributes, "^(prompt|prompt_text|user_system_prompt|full_command|file_path)$")
          - set(attributes["team"], "fe") where attributes["user.email"] == "ada@example.com"
          - set(attributes["team"], "be") where attributes["user.email"] == "bob@example.com"
          - set(attributes["user.hash"], SHA256(Concat([attributes["user.email"], "lab-salt"], ""))) where attributes["user.email"] != nil
          - delete_key(attributes, "user.email")
  batch: {}
exporters:
  debug: { verbosity: detailed }
service:
  extensions: [bearertokenauth]
  pipelines:
    logs: { receivers: [otlp], processors: [transform/scrub, batch], exporters: [debug] }

notes.text: A hard-coded token is fine only in the lab; the real file reads it from the environment.
The same pattern as the real file, minus tool_parameters, so you can see one attribute slip through.
This is what the Terraform loop renders: one set() per email in the team map.
lab-salt stands in for USER_SALT; the hash is still SHA-256 of email plus salt.
The debug exporter prints each record with its attributes; verbosity detailed shows them all.
One logs pipeline, no memory_limiter: the lab sends one record at a time.

lab.title: Run the scrub on your laptop
youNeed: terragrunt (brew install terragrunt), for the reading step

worked.do: mkdir -p ~/scratch/g1-1 && cd ~/scratch/g1-1, save the lab config above as collector.yaml, then: docker network create otel-lab

In a second terminal: docker run --rm --network otel-lab ghcr.io/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/telemetrygen:latest logs --otlp-endpoint otel-lab-collector:4318 --otlp-http --otlp-insecure --otlp-header 'Authorization="Bearer lab-token"' --telemetry-attributes 'prompt="fix the login bug"' --telemetry-attributes 'user.email="ada@example.com"' --telemetry-attributes 'tool_parameters="rm -rf"' --logs 1
worked.see:
INFO  logs/worker.go  logs generated  {"worker": 0, "logs": 1}
INFO  logs/logs.go  stopping the exporter  {"worker": 0}

LogRecord #0
Body: Str(the message)
Attributes:
     -> app: Str(server)
     -> user.hash: Str(86bc3dd67bc04cb396a3b33620dfda2bf4889ac48bca123ff0f5fa319d5e514e)
     -> tool_parameters: Str(rm -rf)

(prompt and user.email are gone; tool_parameters is still there, on purpose)

worked.do: Send again with the same command but without the --otlp-header part
worked.see: FATAL  logs/worker.go  failed to export batched logs  {"error": "failed to send logs to http://otel-lab-collector:4318/v1/logs: 401 Unauthorized ..."}

worked.do: mkdir -p settings && save 20-telemetry.json from the lesson as settings/20-telemetry.json, then: jq -r '.env.OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, .env.OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS' settings/20-telemetry.json

Reading step: mkdir -p otel-collector and save the terragrunt.hcl block as otel-collector/terragrunt.hcl. Then run: terragrunt hcl format --file otel-collector/terragrunt.hcl && terragrunt hcl format --check --file otel-collector/terragrunt.hcl; echo exit $?
worked.see:
exit 0
(the first command realigns the = signs that the dropped blank lines used to separate; --check then passes)

lab.faded: Add tool_parameters to the delete_matching_keys pattern in collector.yaml. Restart the collector (Ctrl-C, then the same docker run) and send the same telemetrygen command. The step left out is the edit to the pattern itself: write it so it matches the real file's pattern exactly. Then the Attributes block must show only app, user.hash and team.
lab.alone: Add a third email, carol@example.com, to team ds in collector.yaml and prove it with one send. Then send a fourth record with an email that is not in the map. Read what happens: no team, a user.hash, and no user.email.
lab.done: The collector prints team and user.hash for every mapped email and never prints prompt, user.email or tool_parameters. A send without the token gets 401.

quiz.q: An engineer sets OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1 on their laptop. Where does the prompt end up?

options.text: In VictoriaLogs, because the flag is per laptop and managed settings cannot stop it
options.why: The flag changes what the laptop sends, but the collector deletes the prompt attribute before export.

options.text: In the WAF's request log at the edge
options.why: The WAF inspects request shapes; it does not store telemetry bodies.

options.text: Nowhere: transform/scrub deletes the prompt attribute before export
options.why: That is why the scrub lives in the collector and G1-02's last step tests exactly this case.

quiz.q: Why does the values template write $${env:INGEST_TOKEN} with two dollar signs?

options.text: Because Terraform's templatefile would read ${ as its own interpolation; $$ leaves a literal ${env:...} for the collector
options.why: The template renders at apply time; the collector resolves env: at start. Two readers, two escapes.

options.text: Because YAML needs a doubled dollar sign inside quotes
options.why: YAML has no special meaning for $; the doubling is for Terraform.

options.text: Because the Helm chart double-escapes environment variables
options.why: The chart passes config through; Terraform is the one that interpolates ${...}.

quiz.q: Where does the real ingest token go?

options.text: Into 20-telemetry.json in RhinoHealth/ai-agents; the repo is private
options.why: The file in git keeps the placeholder; a token in git is a token in every clone.

options.text: Into the claude.ai admin console's server-managed settings, and Vault; never git
options.why: G1-05 says the token is set only in the admin console; Terraform generated it into kvv2.

options.text: Into each engineer's ~/.claude/settings.json by a script
options.why: That is per laptop and overridable; managed settings reach everyone the same way.

words.plain: The OpenTelemetry service that receives telemetry, changes it, and forwards it to a store.
The OpenTelemetry wire protocol; we use its HTTP form with protobuf bodies.
The shared secret every sender presents; it only lets you write telemetry.
A collector step that runs small statements on every record, here to delete and replace attributes.
SHA-256 of a value plus a secret salt: countable, but not reversible without the salt.
A web application firewall at the edge that inspects requests and blocks known attack shapes.
A small tool that sends fake OTLP data, used to test a collector.

tickets.why: Scrubbing in one collector means no prompt, command or file path is stored, even from a misconfigured client.
walk: Create modules/otel-collector: a helm_release of the upstream open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector chart (contrib image, deployment mode, 2 replicas) plus an ExternalSecret from vault-store.

Generate ingest_token and user_salt with Terraform into kvv2 infrastructure/otel-collector, like modules/n8n-secrets. Read the team map from infrastructure/ai-agents/teams with a vault_kv_secret_v2 data source and render it into the values template (code above).
Drop prompt, prompt_text, user_system_prompt, full_command, file_path, tool_parameters and user.email before export. Keep user.hash, a salted SHA-256.
Ask DevOps for -opentelemetry.usePrometheusNaming=true on vminsert. Send logs to the long-term VictoriaLogs. No traces pipeline.
Test from a pod with telemetrygen. Then run one real claude -p session with OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1 on purpose: the prompt must not show up in VictoriaLogs.

tickets.why: Laptops off VPN and agent VMs without peering need one authenticated public address.
walk: Add external_route to the unit (code above): envoy-external, Coraza WAF failing closed like n8n's webhooks, paths /v1/metrics and /v1/logs only.
Leave the token check to the collector (bearertokenauth). The token only lets you write telemetry and reaches people through G1-05.
Test from a laptop off VPN with telemetrygen, with and without the token; expect 401 without it.
Check the WAF does not block protobuf bodies; add a rule exception for the two paths if it does.

tickets.why: Telemetry only helps if everyone sends it the same way, with content off at the source.
walk: Paste the people version into claude.ai server-managed settings with the real ingest token. The token never goes into git.
Leave team unset; the collector turns the email into a team (G1-02).
Agents: the image's copy has no OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and no token. Propose to G3 an OTLP relay in the LLM gateway that checks the run token and adds the ingest token.
Leave OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES and the traces exporter unset.
Check: /status lists the managed source. Within a minute claude_code_cost_usage_USD_total appears in Grafana with a team label and no email.

remember: One address, one token, one scrub: nothing with content is stored, and every number is by team, never by name.
